generate-copy-paid-rows.summary: Copies each Sheet1 row whose column C says Paid to the end of the Paid sheet and reports how many rows were copied.
generate-copy-paid-rows.code:
Option Explicit

' Copies every row of Sheet1 whose Status (column C) is "Paid" to the sheet "Paid".
Private Const SOURCE_SHEET As String = "Sheet1"
Private Const TARGET_SHEET As String = "Paid"
Private Const STATUS_COL As Long = 3

Sub CopyPaidRows()
    Dim src As Worksheet, dst As Worksheet
    Dim lastRow As Long, r As Long, nextRow As Long, copied As Long

    Set src = ThisWorkbook.Worksheets(SOURCE_SHEET)
    Set dst = ThisWorkbook.Worksheets(TARGET_SHEET)
    lastRow = src.Cells(src.Rows.Count, 1).End(xlUp).Row
    nextRow = dst.Cells(dst.Rows.Count, 1).End(xlUp).Row + 1

    For r = 2 To lastRow ' row 1 holds the headers
        If Trim$(CStr(src.Cells(r, STATUS_COL).Value)) = "Paid" Then
            src.Rows(r).Copy Destination:=dst.Rows(nextRow)
            nextRow = nextRow + 1
            copied = copied + 1
        End If
    Next r

    MsgBox copied & " row(s) copied to " & TARGET_SHEET & ".", vbInformation
End Sub
howToRun: Press Alt+F11 to open the VBA editor, then choose Insert > Module.

Save the workbook as .xlsm (macro-enabled) to keep the macro.
assumptions: Column A is filled on every data row, so it is used to find the last row.
"Paid" must match exactly, apart from spaces around it.

generate-outlook-emails.summary: Creates one Outlook email per row of the Mail sheet, using the address, subject and message in columns A to C. It opens each email for checking instead of sending it straight away.
generate-outlook-emails.code:
Option Explicit

' Sends one email per row of the sheet "Mail": A = address, B = subject, C = message.
' Uses Outlook, so it works on Windows with Outlook installed.
Sub SendRowEmails()
    Dim ws As Worksheet, app As Object, mail As Object
    Dim r As Long, lastRow As Long

    Set ws = ThisWorkbook.Worksheets("Mail")
    Set app = CreateObject("Outlook.Application")
    lastRow = ws.Cells(ws.Rows.Count, 1).End(xlUp).Row

    For r = 2 To lastRow
        If Len(ws.Cells(r, 1).Value) > 0 Then
            Set mail = app.CreateItem(0) ' 0 = mail item
            mail.To = ws.Cells(r, 1).Value
            mail.Subject = ws.Cells(r, 2).Value
            mail.Body = ws.Cells(r, 3).Value
            mail.Display ' change to mail.Send once you have checked a few messages
        End If
    Next r
End Sub

generate-delete-old-tmp.summary: Asks for a folder and a confirmation, then deletes the .tmp files in it whose date is more than 30 days ago, and reports how many were deleted.
generate-delete-old-tmp.code:
Option Explicit

' Deletes .tmp files older than 30 days in a folder the user picks.
Sub DeleteOldTmpFiles()
    Dim folder As String, f As String, removed As Long

    With Application.FileDialog(msoFileDialogFolderPicker)
        .Title = "Choose the folder to clean"
        If .Show <> -1 Then Exit Sub
        folder = .SelectedItems(1) & Application.PathSeparator
    End With

    If MsgBox("Delete .tmp files older than 30 days in" & vbCrLf & folder & "?", vbYesNo + vbExclamation) <> vbYes Then Exit Sub

    f = Dir(folder & "*.tmp")
    Do While f <> ""
        If FileDateTime(folder & f) < Now - 30 Then
            Kill folder & f
            removed = removed + 1
        End If
        f = Dir()
    Loop
    MsgBox removed & " file(s) deleted."
End Sub

generate-mac-and-windows.summary: Saves a copy of the workbook in the same folder, named with today's date, using the path separator of the current system so it works on Windows and Mac.
generate-mac-and-windows.code:
Option Explicit

' Saves a copy of this workbook next to it, named with today's date (works on Windows and Mac).
Sub SaveDatedCopy()
    Dim baseName As String, target As String
    baseName = Left$(ThisWorkbook.Name, InStrRev(ThisWorkbook.Name, ".") - 1)
    target = ThisWorkbook.Path & Application.PathSeparator & baseName & "_" & Format(Date, "yyyy-mm-dd") & ".xlsm"
    ThisWorkbook.SaveCopyAs target
    MsgBox "Copy saved as " & target
End Sub

Option Explicit

' Autofits the column widths on every worksheet of this workbook.
Sub AutofitAllColumns()
    Dim ws As Worksheet
